gp.probleme.02: A showcase that spoke about the State, not to citizens
gp.probleme.03: Info.gouv.fr is the entry point for citizens who want to learn about the Government's priority policies. The old page followed an institutional communication logic: four axes with long titles, figures stacked by axis, and actions buried in the text.
gp.probleme.04: The information was there. Finding it took too much effort.
gp.probleme.05: The challengeReconciling regulatory accessibility requirements with a modern experience, without ever leaving the State's design system.
gp.probleme.10: Mockup of the page, scroll through it
gp.probleme.11: Mockup of the old Priority policies page: "Four axes for a fairer and more independent France", then one block per axis with figures and a link to the projects.
gp.probleme.12: Mockup of the redesigned page: "What changes for me", four promises, four priorities as cards with one button each, a clickable map of France and the latest figures.
gp.probleme.13: The page mockups, before and after the redesign. They scroll on their own; hover or touch to take control.
gp.probleme.14: Five knots found during the audit
gp.probleme.16: Too many levels before reaching the information.
gp.probleme.18: The content talked about the institution rather than the service provided.
gp.probleme.20: Nothing guided the eye to the essentials.
gp.probleme.22: Buttons got lost in the editorial text.
gp.probleme.24: Gaps against RGAA and DSFR: sizes, focus, contrasts.
gp.probleme.26: Stay within the State's design system (DSFR)
gp.probleme.27: Meet RGAA: contrasts, keyboard, screen readers
gp.probleme.30: Offer a modern experience despite the framework
gp.comparer.02: Six sites compared, the old Gouvernement.fr included
gp.comparer.03: Before designing, a comparative analysis of European and North American government sites, the old Gouvernement.fr included: what works, what repeats, what is missing.
gp.comparer.05: Task-oriented navigation and benefit-oriented messages for the user.
gp.comparer.06: An entry point, "How can we help you?", that quickly leads to priority services.
gp.comparer.09: A clean design, search first, a clear information architecture.
gp.comparer.10: A complex federal structure to present, with personalised content.
gp.comparer.13: Business domains, clear iconography, explicit calls to action.
gp.comparer.16: Institutional communication, centred on political news.
gp.comparer.18: What the Government wants to say: axes, news, communication.
gp.comparer.20: What citizens come to do: understand what changes for them, and act.
gp.comparer.21: The key finding. Reference sites, GOV.UK and Canada.ca first, start from what users can accomplish rather than from government communication. This reversal is what guided the redesign.

gp.structure.02: A page that answers a single question: what changes for me?
gp.structure.03: The sitemap is tightened, the navigation is shallower, and the page follows the citizen's reading order. In each block, the same hierarchy: a short benefit-oriented title, a proof, an action.
gp.structure.04: The four blocks of the page
gp.structure.09: Introduce yourself in one sentence. The barometer opens with its promise, then four commitments readable at a glance, before any detail.
gp.structure.12: A local impact, in my territory
gp.structure.14: One card per priority. An illustration, a title, a summary, the priority objectives, and a single button: "View the priority".
gp.structure.19: Bringing public action home. A clickable map of France to discover the figures for the State's actions in your region and département.
gp.structure.24: Show it, with a date. The latest updated indicators, each with its date, and access to the data for your region or département.
gp.structure.29: Fewer navigation levels, a tightened sitemap.
gp.structure.31: Citizens read what changes for them, not an administrative label.
gp.structure.33: The same hierarchy in every block of the page.
gp.structure.35: Identifiable, accessible buttons, pulled out of the text.
gp.structure.37: Annotated wireframes designed for mobile, then scaled up.
gp.structure.39: State components and tokens, adapted only when the need requires it.
gp.structure.41: RGAA requires that everything can be done without a mouse, with an always visible focus indicator. The prototypes were checked with the NVDA and VoiceOver screen readers. Move forward with the Tab key (or the button), then remove the visible focus to see what it prevents.

gp.composant.02: A DSFR table, adapted to the barometer
gp.composant.03: To present the barometer results, I helped adapt the DSFR Table component into specific components, built with atomic design and documented for developers. Innovate, yes, but without breaking the consistency of the State's design system.
gp.composant.08: Component example, with three indicators from the final mockup

gp.composant.16: Number of monthly procedures completed at France services
gp.composant.20: Select: Number of MaPrimeRénov' applications approved
gp.composant.23: Select: Number of Service Civique volunteers
gp.composant.26: Three indicators as they appear on the final mockup. Tick a row, then switch to list view: the states and the card view follow the plates below.
gp.composant.27: The four plates of the component
gp.composant.32: "Component elements" plate: cell data types, cell background, cells in SM, MD and LG sizes.
gp.composant.33: Structure. The component's elements, with a clear hierarchy and spacing aligned with DSFR tokens.
gp.composant.34: "Component states" plate: default state and selected row, with bulk actions, Table or List toggle and pagination.
gp.composant.35: States. Default, hover, focus, disabled, selected row: every interactive state meets the RGAA requirements.
gp.composant.36: "Component style" plate: horizontal borders by default, then horizontal and vertical borders.
gp.composant.37: Style. Variants with horizontal or vertical borders, a consistent system typography.
gp.composant.38: "Alternative views" plate: the desktop view as vertical cards, with pagination.
gp.composant.39: Alternative views. A vertical card view for desktop and mobile, so the data stays readable on every screen.
gp.composant.41: Building up a library already in place, from atoms to templates: normalised tokens (typography, spacing, colours) and usage rules per component, when and how, dos and don'ts.
gp.composant.43: A contribution to the technical documentation: responsive rules, component naming, integration examples. Structured wireframes that made the development team's work easier.
gp.composant.45: Sizes, line heights, focus and hover states, contrast ratios: tokens and components adjusted for RGAA, then checked with the keyboard and with NVDA and VoiceOver.

gp.lecons.03: Accessibility, a creative constraintRGAA is not a brake: the contrast and hierarchy requirements pushed me towards sharper choices.
gp.lecons.04: Talk about benefits, not institutionsReplacing institutional titles with what concretely changes for citizens changes how the whole page reads.
gp.lecons.05: Frame together, and earlyThe workshops with business, communication and tech teams aligned all stakeholders early and avoided back and forth at the end of the project.
gp.lecons.06: The design system, an investmentStandardising around the DSFR and enriching the Figma library gives teams a common base for the next pages.
gp.lecons.07: In a public service, every design decision directly affects access to rights and services. This responsibility demands a rigour that goes well beyond aesthetics.
gp.faq.04: UX/UI designer at the Service d'information du Gouvernement (Prime Minister's services) for two years, in a team of designers, PMs, data analysts and developers. I contributed to the redesign with the SIG design team: audit, workshops, wireframes, mockups, prototypes and documentation.
gp.faq.06: The State's design system: the components, tokens and rules shared by public sites. I worked within this framework and helped adapt its Table component for the Priority policies barometer.
gp.faq.08: Through an audit of the gaps (sizes, line heights, focus and hover states, contrasts), fixes recorded in an RGAA audit report, and tests of the prototypes with the NVDA and VoiceOver screen readers.
gp.faq.10: I don't have an export of the site's measurement data. Rather than put forward figures I can't source, this page shows the delivered work, verifiable in the mockups and online.
